pages.title: Path Integral
pages.text: Feynman's insight: a particle takes every possible path at once, and the probabilities add up with phases. Most paths cancel; the classical one survives. The integral shimmers with countless faint trails, all overlapping.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Summing virtual quark trajectories weighted by the Hamiltonian, I found that the straight paths dominated while the rest cancelled. The Analytic Continuator kept them all.
